 Order

This miscellaneous appeal, under section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, has been filed against the Award dated 6/8/2010 passed by Additional Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Ambah, District Morena in Claim Case No. 122/2008.
2.

entities.text: Additional Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Ambah, District Morena
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: As per the case of claimant, respondent no.2 namely Ramnaresh Singh S/o Lotan Singh Rathore was driver of offending vehicle - a Mini Bus bearing registration No. MP-06B/1783.
Respondent no.1 Ashadevi was travelling in the aforesaid vehicle.
It is the case of respondent no.1 that respondent no.2 drove the vehicle in a rash and negligent manner, as a result of which it turned turtle and respondent no.1 sustained grievous injuries.
3. Appellant, as well as, respondent no.2 filed written statements and claimed that no accident took place with the offending vehicle.

Respondent no.3/Insurance Company also denied the claim averments and claimed that NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-GWL:19544 2 MA-1651-2010 respondent no.2 was driving the vehicle without any valid and effective driving licence and, thus,
has violated the terms and conditions of the Insurance Policy.

4. The Claims Tribunal, after recording the evidence of witnesses, held that since driver of the offending vehicle was not having a badge, as required under Rule 8 of Central Motor Vehicle Rules,
therefore, the Insurance Company is not liable as the vehicle was being driven in violation of the Feran Singh vs Ashadevi on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/199080791/
1 Insurance Policy.
5. Challenging the Award passed by the Claims Tribunal, it is submitted by counsel for the appellant that the Tribunal has exonerated the Insurance Company after relying upon judgement passed by Division Bench of Kerala High Court in the case of Govindakutty Nair Vs. Gopalakrishnan reported in 2000 (2) TAC 769 (Kerala) .

entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Govindakutty Nair Vs. Gopalakrishnan reported in 2000 (2) TAC 769 (Kerala)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: However, another Division Bench of the Kerala High Court in the case of P.T.Moidu Vs. Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. and others (2009 ACJ 1104) , after considering the judgement in the case of Govindakutty Nair (Supra), has held that in absence of proof that the insured committed breach by knowingly entrusting the vehicle to a person without badge or absence of badge is the cause of the accident, the Tribunal was justified by directing the Insurance Company to pay the amount of compensation and recover the same from insured.

entities.text: P.T.Moidu Vs. Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. and others (2009 ACJ 1104)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thus, it is submitted that the Insurance Company should not have been exonerated in toto and it should have been held that Insurance Company is liable to pay the compensation amount.

It is further submitted that even otherwise the Tribunal has awarded exorbitant compensation to the injured/respondent NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-GWL:19544 3 MA-1651-2010 no.1.
6 .
Per contra, respondent no.3/Insurance Company has supported the findings recorded by the Tribunal.
7. Heard, learned counsel for the parties.
8. According to the claimants, the driver was having valid licence but he was not having badge to drive the Mini Bus which is a passenger transport vehicle.

The Division Bench of the Kerala High Court in the case of P.T. Modiu (Supra), has held as under:-
"In this case, driver was having a valid driving licence to drive the type of vehicle which he was driving (jeep).

entities.text: Division Bench of the Kerala High Court
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: He was not driving a four wheeler with licence to drive a two wheeler or driving a heavy vehicle with licence to drive a light motor vehicle.
There is no contention for the insurance company, even in the appeal, that absence of the badge is a fundamental breach of policy condition and it is a cause for the accident.

Hence, on the facts of this case, following the dicta laid down in Swaran Singh's case, 2004 ACJ 1 (SC), we are of the opinion that the insurance company cannot be exonerated in indemnifying the owner.

Merely because driver of the vehicle who was duly licensed was not having a badge will not enable the insurance company to shirk its liability as per Section 149 of the Motor Vehicles Act and insurance company also failed to prove that insured has committed a fundamental breach of the policy conditions resulting in the accident.
Hence, we set aside the direction of the tribunal enabling the insurance company to recover the amount after depositing the amount of compensation from the appellant/insured.
Appeal is allowed.
Parties to bear their respective costs."

9. If the facts of present case are considered in the light of judgement passed in P.T.Moidu (Supra) ,
then it is clear from the evidence of S.R.Baghel (DW1) that driver of the offending vehicle was having licence for HTV (Heavy Transport Vehicle), Motorcycle with gear, LMV-NT, which was valid Feran Singh vs Ashadevi on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/199080791/
2 upto 5/9/2009.

However, at the relevant point of time, he was NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2024:MPHC-GWL:19544 4 MA-1651-2010 driving a Mini Bus.

The Supreme Court in the case of Mukund Dewangan v. Oriental Insurance Company Limited reported in (2017) 14 SCC 663 which has been affirmed by the Supreme Court by order dated 8/3/2022 passed in the case of M/s Bajaj Alliance General Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Rambha Devi & Ors. in Civil Appeal No. 841 of 2018

entities.text: Mukund Dewangan v. Oriental Insurance Company Limited reported in (2017) 14 SCC 663
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: M/s Bajaj Alliance General Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Rambha Devi & Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: , has held that in absence of endorsement, it cannot be said that driver of the vehicle was driving the vehicle in violation of terms and conditions of licence.
Merely because respondent no.2 was not having badge as per Rule 8 of the Central Motor Vehicles Rules, it cannot be said that it was the cause of accident.

10. In these circumstances, this Court is of the considered opinion that in the light of law laid down by the Kerala High Court in the case o f P.T.Moidu (Supra) , exoneration of Insurance Company is bad in law.
Accordingly, the Insurance Company is held to be jointly liable to pay the compensation amount.

11. So far as the question of quantum is concerned, The Tribunal has awarded Rs.15,000/- for having suffered injuries, Rs.5000/- towards medical expenses, Rs.1000/- towards special diet and Rs.1,000/- towards physical and mental pain.
By no stretch of imagination it can be said that the aforesaid compensation amount is on a higher side.

12. Accordingly, the Award dated 6/8/2010 passed by Additional Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal,
Ambah, District Morena in Claim case No.122/08 is partially affirmed.
